Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Quibbles 1.1 Components 1.2 Setup 1.3 Goal of the game 1.4 Gameplay 1.4.1 SPLIT/COMBINE 1.4.2 DRAW 1.4.3 ADDING TO COLLECTION 1.4.4 FINALLY 1.5 End of the game 1.6 Expansions 1.6.1 The Magnificent Sevens 1.6.2 The Zero Heroes 1.6.3 The Magnificent Sevens + The Zero Heroes Quibbles 2-5 players, 8+, 5 minutes per player Components 144 cards, numbered 1 to 6: 22×1, 22×2, 22×3, 24×4, 26×5, 28×6 Setup Shuffle the cards thoroughly. Draw 6 cards and put them in a face up row in the middle of the table. Deal every player a hand of 6 cards. Form a face down draw pile from the remaining cards and put it in the middle of the table. Make room for a discard pile. Every player makes room in front of them for a collection of 6 cards. Goal of the game To be the first player to collect cards with a total value of 21 points or more. Gameplay Play in turns. When it is your turn, you first choose to either SPLIT/COMBINE or DRAW. SPLIT/COMBINE Play 1 to 6 cards from your hand with a total value of 6 or less. Put them on the discard pile. Now take cards from the central row on the table in your hands. SPLIT • If you played a single card , you may take all sets of 2 or more cards with the same total value as the card you played. Example: you play a 6 from your hand and now take back a pair of 3s, and a 2+4 set from the table. You leave a 1+5 set on the table, even though you were allowed to take it. Note: every card in the row on the table can only be part of 1 set. COMBINE • If you played 2 or more cards , you may take all single cards with the same value as the total value of the cards you played. Example: play a 1, a 2, and a 3 and take all three 6s from the table. DRAW Add 1 card from your hand face up to the row on the table, draw 2 cards from the draw pile, and put them in your hand. NOTE: There is no hand limit. ADDING TO COLLECTION You may optionally move 1 card from your hand to your collection , for scoring. To do this, you must take all cards of the same value from your hand, with a minimum amount equal to the value of the card. Add one of them to your collection and discard the other cards. In other words : to add a 5 to your collection, you need to have at least five 5s. But for a 2 you only need two 2s. Example: you take all four 4s from your hand, put one 4 in your collection and discard the remaining 4s. You now have no more 4s in your hand. NOTE: you can have only 6 cards in your collection . If you still want to add a card to your collection, you will have to remove one card from your collection first, and put it on the discard pile. FINALLY • Refill the central row to 6 face up cards with cards from the draw pile. • When there are 10 cards in the central row , discard all cards and put 6 new face up cards on the table. • If your hand is empty , all players have to discard the cards they hold in their hands. Deal every player a hand of 6 new cards. Note: if the draw pile is empty, shuffle the discard pile and form a new pile. Now it is the next player’s turn. End of the game You win as soon as you have a collection of six cards with a total value of at least 21 (for instance, a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6). The game ends immediately. Expansions The Magnificent Sevens Add the seven 7 cards to the base game. All basic rules apply, with the following adjustment: When COMBINING , you may play up to 7 cards from your hand, with a total value of 7 or less. The Zero Heroes Add the four 0 cards to the base game. All basic rules apply, with the following adjustments: You cannot SPLIT a 0. [Rating: 3/10] Card game about collecting sets with some new mechanic. But feels weird. Card set collection and efficiency game.

[Rating: 3/10] A charmless little fishing game with a cramped range of card numbers and not much to think about.

[Rating: 3/10] Also für ein strategisches Kartenspiel (zumindest laut Verpackung) ist das eher ein stumpfes Glücksspiel. Die erfolgreichste Strategie scheint tatsächlich einfach nur darin zu bestehen eine Karte aus der Hand abzuwerfen (meist die niedrigste) und dann einfach zwei Karten zu ziehen. Sobald man ein Set voll hat, dieses in der Regel danach rausbringen und wer zuerst sich glücklich gezogen hat gewinnt das Spiel.

[Rating: 3/10] I don’t like the artwork of Quibbles, and the gameplay itself feels like a chore. It’s essentially a straightforward hand management/set collection game, offering nothing new or interesting, but somehow manages to make it even more tedious through constant repetition and grinding. There’s no sense of progression or excitement—just the same motions over and over. Overall, a very dull and forgettable game.

[Rating: 3/10] [i]Bouncing blobs aren’t enough to redeem awkward hand management.[/i] Played in: [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/350958/item/11818925][u]2025[/u][/url]

[Rating: 3/10] After 2 plays on BGA: After the tutorial, I thought I might really like this game. Simple rules, hand management, nothing but numbers and suits, that sounds like the recipe for a quick and breezy game. To my surprise, though, the actual gameplay is incredibly sluggish. The rules feel like a straitjacket: there’s very little you can actually do.  Far too often, the most tempting option is simply to use the fallback action and trade a card for two random ones. It should have been an obvious red flag during playtesting that the game has virtually no flow.  I also don’t like the illustrations. The

[Rating: 4/10] Weird art that I just don't really get, I guess? I think maybe the guys on the cards are Quibbles and so you collect them? Not sure, but it is abstract so it doesn't matter much anyway. I can't quite tell how tactical this actually is, compared to just random. But, either way, my friend group and family would have no interest in a game that is essentially just arithmetic over and over again.
